description: A music video built from cuts, sung to a soundtrack that never touches a chain. The long-take way to film a song - one chained generation lip-synced end to end - degrades with every carried segment and can let the sync slip. This builds the video the way music television does instead: MiniMax-Music3 writes the song, 'slice_audio' cuts it into frame-exact pieces (124 frames at 24 fps each), and every shot is generated fresh from the same Z-Image portrait plus its own slice, lip-synced to just those five seconds. No shot conditions on another shot's output, so the last cut is as clean as the first. 'concat_videos' splices the shots, and because each one covered exactly its slice's frames, the edit is sample-accurate by construction: 'pair_audio' drops the original, unbroken song over the whole cut and the mouths line up in every shot. The generation models pass through one at a time - each is released before the next loads - so the workflow peaks no higher than its largest single model.

variables.singer_portrait_prompt: a 3/4-length portrait of an anthropomorphic river otter lounge singer in a burgundy velvet dinner jacket and black bow tie, standing at a vintage chrome ribbon microphone on a small nightclub stage, a single warm spotlight from above, deep blue darkness behind, photographic, sharp focus
variables.song_prompt: Genre: retro soul jingle, doo-wop tinged. BPM: 92. Key: E-flat major. Emotional progression: warm and wry throughout, swelling on the hook. Listening scenario: a late-night variety show number. Production profile: vintage, close-mic, plate reverb, slightly warm tape saturation. Vocals: smooth male crooner lead, velvety and unhurried, small melisma on the hook. Arrangement: upright bass and brushed drums under electric piano, a two-note baritone sax riff answering each line, finger snaps on the backbeat. The hook lands twice and the last line is held.

He sings the vocal of <Audio 1>, his mouth moving in natural synchronisation with it, one paw resting on the microphone stand and the other loose at his side, swaying gently with the tempo.
